prompt:
A smooth sphere P of mass 0.300 kg slides horizontally at 5.00 m s^-1 along the positive x-axis on a frictionless table and collides with a stationary identical sphere Q of mass 0.300 kg.
After the collision, sphere P moves with speed 3.50 m s^-1 at an angle of 30.0 degrees above the positive x-axis (positive y-direction).

(a) Calculate the initial momentum of sphere P before the collision. [1]
(b) Calculate the x-component and y-component of the momentum of sphere P after the collision. [2]
(c) By applying the principle of conservation of linear momentum:
(i) Determine the y-component of the momentum of sphere Q after the collision. [1]
(ii) Calculate the magnitude and direction of the velocity of sphere Q after the collision. [2]

response_structure.description: Components of momentum of sphere P after collision
y-component of momentum of sphere Q
Velocity magnitude and direction of sphere Q

hints: Use p = mv along the x-axis.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: p_initial = 0.300 kg x 5.00 m s^-1 = 1.50 kg m s^-1.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting the unit kg m s^-1 or N s.

hints: Find the momentum of sphere P first: p_P = m v_P = 0.300 x 3.50.
Resolve into components using cos(30 deg) and sin(30 deg).
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Total momentum of P = 0.300 x 3.50 = 1.050 kg m s^-1.
Step 2: x-component p_Px = 1.050 cos(30.0 deg) = 1.050 x 0.8660 = 0.909 kg m s^-1.
Step 3: y-component p_Py = 1.050 sin(30.0 deg) = 1.050 x 0.5000 = 0.525 kg m s^-1.
common_pitfalls: Swapping sin and cos between the axes.
Omitting the negative sign or direction.

hints: Use conservation along x: p_initial = p_Px + p_Qx to find p_Qx.
Combine p_Qx and p_Qy with Pythagoras to find total p_Q, then divide by mass.
Calculate the angle using arctan(p_Qy / p_Qx).
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: p_Qx = p_initial - p_Px = 1.500 - 0.9093 = 0.5907 kg m s^-1.
Step 4: Angle theta = arctan(0.525 / 0.5907) = arctan(0.8888) = 41.6 deg below positive x-axis.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting to divide momentum by mass to find velocity.
Calculating magnitude only and failing to give direction.

hints: Momentum is conserved independently along the x and y axes.
Initial y-momentum is zero, so final y-momenta must be equal and opposite.
solution:
(a) p_initial = 0.300 kg x 5.00 m s^-1 = 1.50 kg m s^-1 along positive x-axis.
(b) Total momentum of P = 0.300 x 3.50 = 1.050 kg m s^-1.
p_Px = 1.050 cos(30.0 deg) = 0.909 kg m s^-1.
p_Py = 1.050 sin(30.0 deg) = 0.525 kg m s^-1.
(c)(i) Initial y-momentum is zero, so p_Qy = -p_Py = -0.525 kg m s^-1 (0.525 kg m s^-1 in the negative y-direction).
(c)(ii) Conservation along x: p_Qx = 1.50 - 0.9093 = 0.5907 kg m s^-1.
Total momentum p_Q = sqrt(0.5907^2 + (-0.525)^2) = 0.790 kg m s^-1.
Speed v_Q = 0.790 / 0.300 = 2.63 m s^-1.
Direction: angle theta = arctan(0.525 / 0.5907) = 41.6 deg below the positive x-axis.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 4: (c)(ii) p_Qx = 1.50 - 0.9093 = 0.5907 kg m s^-1; p_Q = 0.790 kg m s^-1; v_Q = 2.63 m s^-1 at 41.6 deg below x-axis.

mark_scheme.criterion: -0.525 kg m s^-1 (accept 0.525 kg m s^-1 downwards / in negative y-direction)
Speed = 2.63 m s^-1 at an angle of 41.6 deg below positive x-axis (accept 42 deg)
